title: Don’t Curse the World
text: Every time, my father looks surprised when it comes to using slaves.
“Slaves are branded with a ‘slave mark’—a symbol that causes them pain if they disobey, making it impossible for them to betray their master.”
The same goes for monster marks, doesn’t it? Well, the Filolial-sama are generally obedient folk who rarely disobey. It might be a good way to control pigs, don’t you think?
“B-but I can’t do something so cruel.”
“We’ve had this conversation before. However, in the first timeline, my future Father had no trustworthy companions, so he ended up using slaves.”
My Big Sister was Father’s first slave, wasn’t she? I was swayed by the Crimson Swine’s whispers and, without realizing that Father and my Big Sister were building a bond, tried to tear them apart.
“And he was making money by putting his slaves to work, wasn’t he? In exchange for protecting them from monsters, he left all the monster-hunting to them.”
“In a situation where I can’t attack and Motoyasu-kun isn’t here to help me like this… I suppose that’s probably the only thing to do…”
My father is clutching Sakura-chan’s egg.
“Hey, can’t we have this kid help out as a salesperson or something?”
“Well, that depends on Filolial-sama’s personality… Future Sakura-chan was good at protecting her Father, but I’m not sure how she’d handle running a business.”

Even in my group, Midori was about the only one who really understood Father’s business. Filolial-sama generally loves having fun, but I think she’s a bit clueless when it comes to dealing with people in business.
“Ugh…”
“What? You don’t need to worry.”
“Why not?”
“Father taught the slaves to defeat monsters with a smile, so with his skills, managing slaves should be a breeze. He used to command more slaves than there were people in an entire village.”
“Now I’m even more worried!”
Father stood up and shouted.
“What? Just how much of a monster had my future self become? Forcing slaves to fight, and making them kill monsters cheerfully as if they’d been brainwashed…”
Oh? It seems my Father has misunderstood a bit. I must tell him the truth.
“That’s not true, Father.”
“What do you mean, it’s not true?”

“They were all… people who, upon learning of your mission to challenge the waves, volunteered to help. You, Father, used your delicious cooking—which draws people in—to… win over their stomachs and awaken them to their mission.”
“That just sounds like you’re rephrasing it; the substance doesn’t seem to have changed at all.”
That’s odd, isn’t it? Did I say something strange? But everyone—starting with the slaves and including the Filolial-sama—was eager for your cooking, Father.
Above all, Filo-tan was really looking forward to Father’s cooking. Food is vitality, you know. As I recall, what Father set out to build was a place where everyone could do what they wanted to do.
“Well… it seems no one’s willing to join me, and recruiting people from the Demi-Human kingdom would only increase the danger… so I guess there’s no helping it.”
Father nods reluctantly and looks up.
“It might be fine if it were just about level and equipment, but isn’t one of your goals also to boost your reputation in this country through your trading?”

“That’s true. When the Father was wanted, it was partly because of the great deeds he’d accomplished in various regions that made it difficult to track him down, but it also seemed like the people of the country truly trusted him.”

It reminds me of the time we were tricked by the Crimson Swine and were chasing him. Back then, it was extremely difficult to determine where my Father had fled. Not only did the people cause confusion by claiming to have seen the Shield Hero in various towns, but once they learned that the Shield Hero was the Saint of the Divine Bird, they seemed to say that even if a saint were the Shield Hero, his great deeds would remain the same.

I remember Crimson Swine venting his frustration to me. Crimson Swine, the Pope, and Trash all claimed, “He manipulated the people with brainwashing!” But as someone who knows the future, I can say with certainty that the truth is it was all thanks to my Father’s tireless efforts.
“I see… If I go around as a peddler and earn the people’s trust… I might be able to make it work.”
“Exactly.”

“Alright. Whether it’s buying slaves or peddling goods, I’ll try to put up with it, even though I don’t like it. I’m not exactly without anxiety about whether I can actually take care of someone, though.”
“That’s exactly what makes you my Father.”
Now, what should I talk to my Father about? While I was thinking about it, my Father spoke up.
“So, what should I do first? If there are any methods or tips for getting stronger, I’d like you to teach me.”
“That’s right! I must teach you how to enhance your weapons.”
“Huh? Can’t I just read the Help section thoroughly?”

“The enhancement methods listed in the Help section are only a tiny fraction of the whole. Each hero’s weapon contains its own unique enhancement method, and by building trust with the weapon, those methods combine to make it stronger.”
“R-really? It’s quite a complex system, isn’t it?”

I went ahead and taught my Father the enhancement methods. Of course, since it would take time to teach everything, I limited myself to giving him a brief overview of what’s available. After all, he’ll probably be missing quite a few things as he tries them out.
“Hmm… Looks like I’ll just have to do my best.”
“However, there’s one thing I’d like you to remember well.”
“What?”

“I’ve tried to act as closely as possible to how things were in the first world, but by siding with you, Father, things have started to differ. In the first world, it seems you weren’t often attacked by enemy assassins…”
“Hmm… Even so, that’s still a million times better than cursing a world where I have no allies at all… I’ll tough it out.”

My Father quietly closed his eyes, then looked at me and replied. For the time being, what we need to do is secretly raise Father’s level. To do that, training Filolial-sama is essential… and we’ll need to secure slave salespeople to work in Father’s place while he’s out peddling.

Father could act as a salesperson himself, but there’s a risk of price haggling and unwanted negative rumors, so I suppose we have no choice. …I remember my Father peddling goods in the first world… but I also seem to recall there were other problems as well. Well… I’ll just have to ask about that somewhere.
“Alright, let’s get my Father some clothes… or armor, and get started.”
“Yeah, you’re right.”
Yuki-chan and Kou chirped cheerfully. Well then, this is where we really have to give it our all.
“Oh? Are you two done talking, An-chan and the others?”
“Yes. Sorry for having you prepare a room for us.”
“Don’t worry about it. By the way, you look a bit shabby in that outfit, don’t you? Since you were stripped of everything—and if your chainmail was stolen too—how about I give you some for free?”
I know the old man at the weapon shop is a very kind-hearted fellow who was a favorite of my Father’s. The first time I looped back, he’d been just as considerate toward my Father.
“…No, it’s fine. I don’t need the chainmail.”
We’d had this exchange before, too.
“Still, you’ll look even worse in just your undershirt.”
“My future Father bought leather armor here. So please, I’d like you to sell it to him with this money.”
I showed the money pouch to the old man at the weapon shop. After all, I’d saved this money specifically for this. Buying what you need, in the amount you need—that, too, is essential for battle.
“Oh, come on! If you don’t have enough money, even cheap clothes would be fine…”
“Don’t worry about it. Appearance is important, you know.”
“I… see. Alright, then.”
“Is everything settled, An-chan? You’ve got some great companions here. By the way, Spear-An-chan… aren’t you going to wear anything?”
“I’m all set.”
“Huh? Motoyasu, aren’t you going to buy armor?”
“I’m just putting Father first. Once I have some extra money, I’ll get my own gear too.”
“I’m always causing you trouble with everything… I’m sorry.”
“There’s no need to be shy around us.”
At my father’s words, Father wiped away his tears—which had brought him to the brink of tears—and nodded.
“Yeah, I’ll do my best to live up to the trust Motoyasu-kun and Dad have placed in me.”
“Hahaha, you’re a little unreliable, but give it your best shot!”
With that, he picked out a leather suit of armor for my Father. It looks a bit on the cheaper side.
“Now then, Father. I have one more favor to ask of the weapon shop owner.”
“Hm? Is there more?”
“Actually…”
